hints.content: The arrow points to all values less than $-6$.
So, the inequality represents everything **less than $-6$.**

question.content:
**Choose the inequality that represents the following graph.**



[[☃ image 1]]

[[☃ radio 1]]

options.alt: A number line from negative 9 to 1 with evenly spaced tick marks in increments of 1. An open point is plotted at negative 6. A line running to the left starts at negative 6 and continues.

choices.clue:
The graph of $-6<x$ actually looks like this:

![A number line from negative 9 to 1 with evenly spaced tick marks in increments of 1. An open point is plotted at negative 6. A line running to the right starts at negative 6 and continues.](web+graphie:${☣ LOCALPATH}/images/cc183000aaa2fac158df2b2a42a3f61377d2cc9b)

The graph of $-5<x$ actually looks like this:

![A number line from negative 9 to 1 with evenly spaced tick marks in increments of 1. An open point is plotted at negative 5. A line running to the right starts at negative 5 and continues.](web+graphie:${☣ LOCALPATH}/images/122c8404823369e5fc4ece8e2198393bd4df1d92)

The graph of $-5>x$ actually looks like this:

![A number line from negative 9 to 1 with evenly spaced tick marks in increments of 1. An open point is plotted at negative 5. A line running to the left starts at negative 5 and continues.](web+graphie:${☣ LOCALPATH}/images/2fcd9d2b9dfedbc890aa14a338b5b05097028f7a)
